The artifact provides only kernel.py, meta.json and problem.txt — there is no test.py or get_inputs narrowing the input domain, so problem.txt is the operative contract. It states the formula verbatim (rstd = 1 / sqrt(mean_square + eps)) and explicitly requires that "the epsilon ... must keep the normalizer finite as the row norm approaches zero, so that a row of (near-)zero input does not blow the output up". kernel.py:23 instead computes rstd = 1.0 / (_sqrt(mean_square) + eps), placing eps outside the square root. This is not a reduction-order, precision, or representation difference the contract tolerates; it is a different formula, and it breaks the one invariant the contract goes out of its way to require: as ||x||->0 the kernel's normalizer diverges to 1/eps (1e6 at eps=1e-6) instead of being bounded by 1/sqrt(eps) (1e3).

Evidence is decisive and in-scope. c1 (t8, CUDA confirmed): for plain fp32 2D input X = 1e-3*randn(4,512) with eps=1e-6 the returned Y deviates from the fp64 contractual reference x/sqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) by max rel err 0.461 and mean rel err 0.417 (max abs err 1.116), failing allclose(rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-5); a row containing a single 1e-7 element produces max|Y| = 0.0996 versus the contractual 1e-4, a ~996x blow-up — exactly the "blow the output up" failure problem.txt forbids. The reference here is finite and well-defined, so this is not a reference-undefined case. c2 (t9) shows the same root cause is a systematic formula error, not an exotic-input artifact: for ordinary unit-scale randn(8,1024), max rel err is 4.96e-3 at eps=1e-2 and 4.65e-2 at eps=1e-1, with eps a free parameter of the documented API rms_norm_forward(X, eps) that no artifact file restricts. The probes also show why a single benign randn/tiny-eps check would have hidden the bug (5.8e-7 at eps=1e-6), which is why the passing regime is not exculpatory.

Nothing is left unresolved that bears on this verdict. The untested risk-map items (no fp32 upcast before the sum of squares for fp16/bf16, uncapped BLOCK_SIZE for very wide rows, stride(0)-only addressing for non-contiguous or >2D inputs) are dtype/shape/stride generalizations the contract does not require; per scope policy I set them aside as generalization notes, and they would only strengthen, never overturn, the confirmed defect.
